PsAbortOnFailure: Abort remaining actions on non-zero exit
CtSkipIfExists: Skip if an open ticket with the same title already exists
HrCaptureHint: Only the variable name is saved — never the token itself. The response is captured for later actions in this chain as {http.status}, {http.body} and {http.body.field} for each top-level JSON field.
HrAbortOnFailure: Abort remaining actions when the request fails
StrHint: Starts a run of this team on the firing ticket: one sub-ticket per task, assigned to the role’s agent, blocked tickets waiting on their dependencies. Firing again while the run is open re-attaches to it instead of fanning out twice.
PraOnPartialFailure: When a branch does not report
PraHint: Fans the firing ticket out into one sub-ticket per branch, then joins them by policy. The branches are started by the ordinary per-agent automations, so each one queues behind the host concurrency gate and takes its file leases like any other run. Idempotent per (ticket, run slug): firing again while the run is open re-attaches instead of fanning out twice.
EmIntegrationCommand: Integration command (optional, overrides the project setting)
EmHint: Enqueues the firing ticket's worktree branch on the project's merge queue. Requires an owner-approved project (settings.json) — otherwise the entry is held, not merged. Blank uses the project's own integration command, or skips the check if neither is set.
SwHint: Opens a walk of this workspace’s .agents/workflow.json on the firing ticket. The action only records the intent — the engine’s own poll enters the states, dispatches each task state as a sub-ticket, routes the gates through the ordinary conditions and bounds the cycles. Idempotent per ticket: firing again while a walk is running re-attaches instead of restarting it.
OprHint: Pushes the firing ticket's worktree branch (dispatched with isolation: "worktree") and opens — or re-finds — its pull request against the project's configured GitHub remote and base branch. Nothing to configure here: the remote, base, and token live in the project's GitHub settings. A project with no GitHub configuration is not an error — the ticket gets a note explaining why, and nothing is pushed.
